whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the Tableau Server Administrator exam for?

personas.label: IT Administrators
personas.description: Professionals responsible for deploying, configuring, and maintaining Tableau Server or Tableau Cloud environments for their organization.

personas.label: System Administrators
personas.description: Admins managing user provisioning, authentication (SAML, LDAP, Active Directory), and security policies for Tableau Server.

personas.label: Operations Teams
personas.description: Teams monitoring server health, managing extract refresh schedules, troubleshooting failures, and performing backup and recovery.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Tableau Server Administrator Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The Tableau Server Administrator exam is moderately difficult. It requires fluency with TSM commands, server process architecture, and real troubleshooting scenarios — studying documentation without hands-on server management experience leaves significant gaps.
bullets: 45 questions in 90 minutes — roughly two minutes per question, which is manageable for candidates familiar with the admin interface.
~70% passing score — you need approximately 32 correct answers out of 45 to pass.
TSM command-line fluency is essential — the exam tests specific TSM operations for configuration, backup, restore, and maintenance.
Hands-on server administration helps most — candidates who have managed extract refreshes, configured authentication, and used Admin Views pass at higher rates.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Book when you can confidently run TSM commands, troubleshoot failed extract refreshes, configure SAML SSO, and interpret Admin Views without looking up steps.

examFormat.heading: Tableau Server Administrator Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or in-person. Here is the format:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Scenario questions describe server issues — failed extract refreshes, slow dashboard loads, authentication errors — and ask you to identify the correct diagnostic or resolution step.
bestWayToPass: TSM commands: Memorize key TSM operations — tsm status, tsm configuration set/get, tsm maintenance backup/restore, and tsm restart.
Process architecture: Know what each Tableau Server process does (VizQL, Backgrounder, Data Server, Repository) and which logs to check when it fails.
Authentication configuration: Understand SAML SSO, Active Directory sync, OpenID Connect, and Kerberos setup, including common troubleshooting steps.
Admin Views: Practice using built-in monitoring dashboards (Background Tasks, Traffic to Views, Stats for Space Used) for proactive maintenance.

certificationCard.description: Tableau Server Administrators deploy, configure, and manage Tableau Server and Tableau Cloud. They handle installation, security, user management, sites, and performance.

keyConcepts.h2: Tableau Server Administrator: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Tableau Server Architecture and Processes
blocks.body: Tableau Server runs as a set of processes that can be distributed across multiple nodes. Key processes: VizQL Server (renders views), Application Server (handles web requests, API calls), Data Server (manages data connections and caching), Backgrounder (runs extract refreshes, subscriptions, flows), Data Engine (stores and queries Hyper extract files), Repository (PostgreSQL — stores user, content, and workgroup metadata). Single-node deployments run all processes on one machine. Multi-node clusters distribute processes for scale and redundancy.

blocks.heading: Installation, Configuration, and TSM
blocks.body: Tableau Services Manager (TSM) is the command-line and web UI administration tool for Tableau Server. tsm configuration set changes server settings. tsm maintenance backup/restore handles server backup and recovery. TSM web UI provides a graphical interface for common admin tasks. Installation: requires a dedicated server, admin user, and product key. Initial configuration: server admin account, authentication mode (local, Active Directory, **SAML**), SSL/TLS certificate upload. Identity store: Local (Tableau manages users), Active Directory (sync from AD), or LDAP.

blocks.heading: User Management and Licensing
blocks.body: Site Roles determine what users can do: Creator (can create and publish workbooks, edit in web), Explorer (can view and interact, limited edit), Viewer (view only). User limit is set by the licence type. Active Directory group sync automates user management — AD group membership maps to Tableau site roles. Multi-site Tableau Server can have users assigned to multiple sites with different roles per site. Licensing compliance: the admin monitors licence usage and usage reports to ensure the organisation stays within licence limits.

blocks.heading: Content Management: Projects and Permissions
blocks.body: Projects organise content (workbooks, data sources, flows) in a hierarchy. Top-level projects and nested projects support complex permission models. Permission capabilities: View, Download, Edit, Publish, Connect, Move, Delete — each can be Allowed, Denied, or Inherited. Permissions inherit from the project to its content — child projects inherit from parent unless overridden. Locking project permissions prevents users from changing content permissions. The admin designs the project hierarchy to match organisational structure and governance requirements.

blocks.heading: Monitoring, Maintenance, and Troubleshooting
blocks.body: Admin Views are built-in dashboards for monitoring server health: Background Tasks, User Activity, Traffic to Views, Disk Space. tsm jobs commands manage and monitor background tasks. Log files in ProgramData/Tableau capture detailed process activity — useful for troubleshooting failed extract refreshes, slow view rendering, and authentication issues. Tableau Server repository (PostgreSQL) can be queried for advanced analytics on server usage. Scheduled extract refreshes: the admin monitors success rates and investigates failures (data source credentials, network issues, query timeouts).

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Tableau Server Certified Administrator Exam
scenarioTips.intro: The Tableau Server Administrator exam tests server administration skills: installation, configuration, performance monitoring, and troubleshooting. Focus on TSM commands, backup/restore, and user management at scale.

blocks.heading: TSM Command-Line Interface
blocks.body: Know key TSM commands: tsm status, tsm configuration set/get, tsm restart, tsm maintenance backup/restore, and tsm sites export/import. Administrators need command-line fluency for the exam.

blocks.heading: User & Content Management
blocks.body: Know how to manage users (local vs. Active Directory), site roles and their capabilities, groups, and how to bulk-import users with CSV. Understand how to configure site limits (storage, user counts).

blocks.heading: Performance Monitoring
blocks.body: Know how to use Tableau Server's built-in monitoring: the Admin views (Background Tasks, Stats for Space Used, Traffic to Views), Resource Monitoring Tool (RMT), and PostgreSQL repository queries.

blocks.heading: Backup & Recovery
blocks.body: Know how to configure backup schedules using TSM, what is included in a TSM backup (content, configuration, PostgreSQL), and how to restore from backup including the recovery process for failed nodes.

blocks.heading: Authentication Configuration
blocks.body: Know how to configure local authentication, Active Directory/LDAP, **SAML** **SSO**, OpenID Connect, and Kerberos. Understand how authentication method affects user provisioning and session management.

sampleQuestions.question: Which command-line tool is used to change Tableau Server configuration and restart services?
options: tsm
psql
tableau-desktop
tabcmd
sampleQuestions.explanation: TSM manages the server platform itself, including configuration, topology and service control.
whyWrong: psql is a PostgreSQL client and is not the supported administration tool.
Tableau Desktop is the authoring client.
tabcmd automates content tasks such as publishing and exporting, not platform configuration.

sampleQuestions.question: Which tool would an administrator script to publish a workbook or export a view to PDF on a schedule?
options: tabcmd
tsm
The Backgrounder process directly
The repository database
sampleQuestions.explanation: tabcmd performs content-level operations and is the usual choice for scripting them.
whyWrong: TSM configures the platform rather than manipulating content.
Processes are not invoked directly by administrators.
Writing to the repository directly is unsupported.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Tableau Server process executes scheduled extract refreshes and subscriptions?
options: VizQL Server
Backgrounder
Repository
Gateway
sampleQuestions.explanation: Backgrounder runs background tasks, which is where extract refreshes and subscription deliveries happen.
whyWrong: VizQL Server renders views for interactive users.
The Repository stores metadata and does not execute tasks.
Gateway handles incoming requests and routing.

sampleQuestions.question: Users report that dashboards are slow to load interactively, while scheduled refreshes complete on time. Which process is the first place to look?
options: Backgrounder
VizQL Server
The TSM controller
The licensing service
sampleQuestions.explanation: Interactive rendering is VizQL Server's work, and healthy scheduled refreshes point away from Backgrounder.
whyWrong: Backgrounder handles the scheduled work that is already completing normally.
The TSM controller manages administration, not view rendering.
Licensing affects access rather than render speed.

sampleQuestions.question: Extract refreshes are queuing and finishing late, while interactive performance is fine. What is the most appropriate response?
options: Add more VizQL Server processes to the node
Switch the server to a different authentication method
Reduce the number of sites on the installation
Add Backgrounder capacity or spread the schedules
sampleQuestions.explanation: Late background work with healthy interactive performance indicates Backgrounder capacity or scheduling is the constraint.
whyWrong: VizQL Server affects interactive rendering, which is not the problem described.
Authentication is unrelated to refresh capacity.
Site count does not govern refresh throughput.

sampleQuestions.question: A user must publish workbooks and control permissions on their own projects, but must not administer the site. What should be granted?
options: The Server Administrator role for the installation
A publishing site role plus project leader on those projects
No licence, with access granted by group
The Viewer role on every project
sampleQuestions.explanation: Publishing comes from the site role, and authority over specific projects comes from being project leader on them.
whyWrong: Server Administrator grants control of the whole installation, far more than required.
An unlicensed user cannot sign in to work with content.
Viewer cannot publish content.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the effect of locking permissions to a project?
options: Content inherits the project's permissions, with no per-item override
The project is hidden from all search results
Extract refreshes for content in the project pause
The project becomes read-only for every user
sampleQuestions.explanation: Locking enforces the project's permission model on everything inside it, preventing per-workbook divergence.
whyWrong: Visibility is controlled by permissions, not by the lock setting.
Scheduling is unaffected by permission locking.
Locking governs who sets permissions, not whether content can be edited.

sampleQuestions.question: An administrator must take a full backup that can restore the server's content and metadata. Which TSM operation produces it?
options: tsm maintenance backup
tabcmd get
tsm status
tsm maintenance cleanup
sampleQuestions.explanation: The maintenance backup command produces the archive containing the repository and extract data.
whyWrong: tabcmd get downloads a single piece of content.
tsm status reports service state.
Cleanup removes logs and temporary files rather than creating a backup.

sampleQuestions.question: What does tsm maintenance cleanup do?
options: Creates a restore point for the installation
Rebuilds the server's content search index
Reassigns site roles across every site
Removes old logs and temporary files
sampleQuestions.explanation: Cleanup reclaims disk space by deleting logs and temporary files.
whyWrong: Restore points come from a backup, not from cleanup.
Index rebuilding is a separate maintenance action.
Site roles are managed through the web interface or the API.

sampleQuestions.question: After configuring an external identity provider, users can reach the sign-in page but authentication fails. Where should the administrator look first?
options: The Backgrounder queue
Workbook permissions for the affected users
The identity provider and certificate trust settings
The extract refresh schedule for the source
sampleQuestions.explanation: Authentication failures at sign-in point to the identity provider configuration and the certificate trust between it and the server.
whyWrong: The Backgrounder queue concerns scheduled tasks rather than sign-in.
Permissions apply after a user has authenticated.
Refresh schedules are unrelated to authentication.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of creating multiple sites on one Tableau Server installation?
options: To provide a backup of the content
To increase extract refresh throughput per node
To separate content and users on shared hardware
To enable multi-factor authentication
sampleQuestions.explanation: Sites partition content and user access within a single installation.
whyWrong: Sites are not a backup mechanism.
Throughput depends on process capacity rather than site count.
Authentication methods are configured at the server level.

sampleQuestions.question: Which statement about licensing is correct?
options: All site roles consume the same licence tier
Viewers do not require a licence
Licences are tiered by site role, Creator highest
Licensing is configured per project
sampleQuestions.explanation: Licences are tiered, and the role assigned determines which tier a user consumes.
whyWrong: Roles consume different licence tiers.
Viewers require a Viewer licence.
Licensing is an installation-level concern, not per project.

sampleQuestions.question: An administrator needs to see which views are used least often, to plan content cleanup. Where should they look?
options: The workbook XML of each published workbook
The gateway request log entries only
The TSM configuration file on each node
The built-in administrative views
sampleQuestions.explanation: Administrative views report usage, performance and content activity, which is what usage analysis needs.
whyWrong: Workbook XML describes a single workbook's definition.
Gateway logs record requests but are not a usage report.
Configuration files describe setup, not usage.

sampleQuestions.question: A published data source needs credentials so scheduled refreshes can run without a user present. What should be configured?
options: A new site for the data source
Embedded credentials on the data source
A higher site role for all viewers
Prompting the user at refresh time
sampleQuestions.explanation: Scheduled refreshes run with no user present, so the connection credentials must be stored with the data source.
whyWrong: Creating a site does not supply credentials.
Raising site roles does not authenticate to the underlying database.
Prompting cannot work when no user is present.

sampleQuestions.question: What should an administrator do before applying a configuration change that requires a service restart in production?
options: Apply it immediately during peak hours
Delete old workbooks first
Back up, then apply it in a maintenance window
Switch all users to Viewer
sampleQuestions.explanation: Changes that restart services interrupt users, so a backup and a planned window are the standard precautions.
whyWrong: Restarting during peak hours causes avoidable disruption.
Content deletion is unrelated to applying a configuration change.
Changing site roles does not reduce restart impact.
